name: Lip liner overlining
summary: Drawing liner just outside the lip line to suggest fuller lips; a long-standing makeup technique with no trials behind its effect.
lead: Overlining is a makeup technique in which a lip liner pencil is drawn slightly outside the natural lip border, and the space is filled with lip color, to create the appearance of fuller or larger lips . Wikipedia's article on lip liner describes this effect without using the term, noting that liner sharpens the boundary between lips and skin so that lips look more prominent .

name: Plumping gloss (menthol / cinnamon)
summary: Irritant glosses that swell lips for a short-lived fuller look; little formal research behind them.
lead: Lip plumpers are cosmetics that make lips look fuller by irritating the lip skin and causing temporary swelling . Wikipedia names capsaicin, the compound in chili peppers, as an ingredient; it does not discuss menthol or cinnamon-based products specifically .

name: Lip scrub exfoliation
summary: Abrasive scrub for flaky lips; no studies, and dermatologists describe exfoliation as optional.
lead: A lip scrub is an abrasive product, commonly sugar- or salt-based, used to rub flaking skin off the lips. It is a form of mechanical exfoliation, in which abrasives such as sugar or salt crystals, cloths or brushes physically remove surface skin cells .

name: Lip balm / petrolatum slugging
summary: Occlusive balm or petrolatum to keep lips from chapping; routine care, not a trial-tested appearance fix.
lead: Lip balm is a wax-based topical product that forms an occlusive layer over the lips to seal in moisture and relieve chapping. Common bases include beeswax, carnauba or candelilla wax, lanolin, paraffin and petrolatum, sometimes with flavor, color, camphor or sunscreen . Petrolatum (petroleum jelly) used alone is a widely used skin protectant, and applying a thick layer overnight is called slugging in skincare culture .
claims: Lip balm can make eyebrows look thicker.

name: Lip mask (overnight)
summary: Thick overnight occlusive for lips; standard moisturizing care with no appearance trials.
lead: An overnight lip mask is a thick, occlusive lip treatment left on during sleep, in the same category as lip balm and petroleum jelly, which form a barrier that slows moisture loss from the lips . Overnight balms are described as using thicker emollients such as lanolin for longer moisture retention . Wikipedia notes that medical-grade lanolin can speed healing of chapped lips .

name: Shot glass lip challenge
summary: A viral suction trick that swells the lips for a short time; no studies exist and bruising is the commonly reported result.
lead: The shot glass lip challenge is a social-media trend in which people press the rim of a small glass or similar container over their mouth and create suction, so that the lips swell temporarily and look fuller. It is a do-it-yourself variant of suction lip plumping, which medical references describe as drawing blood into the lips by vacuum pressure and producing short-lived swelling.

name: Tinted lip balm for men
summary: Moisturising balm with a sheer wash of colour; a low-stakes grooming product with no appearance trials.
lead: Tinted lip balm is a hybrid cosmetic that combines the moisturising and protective role of ordinary lip balm with a sheer, buildable wash of colour. Men who use it are generally seeking a subtly healthier or more even lip tone without the opacity of lipstick; the entry is treated here as part of grooming and style culture.

name: Hyaluron pen (needle-free)
summary: A high-pressure needle-free filler injector sold for DIY lips; the FDA warns against it and surveys report frequent complications.
lead: The hyaluron pen is a handheld needle-free device that uses compressed air or a spring mechanism to force hyaluronic acid filler through the skin surface, mainly for lip augmentation and wrinkles. It has been promoted online for at-home use.
claims: It gives lip filler results without needles or pain.
It is a safe at-home alternative to a clinic.

name: Lip hydration / water intake
summary: Water and humid air for smoother lips; plausible and low-risk but with little direct research.
lead: Lip hydration, as discussed in appearance communities, covers drinking water, humidifying indoor air and similar habits to keep lips smooth and less dry. Research notes that the vermilion lip is particularly susceptible to water loss.

name: Lip microneedling
summary: Needling aimed at lip lines and volume; established for scars elsewhere but unstudied on lips.
lead: Lip microneedling applies the collagen induction technique, repeated puncturing of the skin with tiny sterile needles, to the lip area, with proponents aiming at finer lines and modest volume. General microneedling is used for scarring and acne, and research on it is described as ongoing.

name: CO2 laser perioral rejuvenation
summary: Clinic laser resurfacing for lip lines; established technique with registered trials, but downtime and scarring risks apply.
lead: CO2 laser perioral rejuvenation uses a carbon dioxide laser to treat lines around the mouth. CO2 lasers emit at 10,600 nm, vaporise tissue and heat the deep dermis, which is thought to stimulate collagen and elastin production.

name: Hyaluronidase lip filler dissolving
summary: An enzyme injected to break down hyaluronic acid filler in the lips; the standard reversal route, though evidence here is mostly clinical practice rather than trials.
lead: Hyaluronidase is a family of enzymes that break down hyaluronic acid, a sugar-based polymer found naturally in connective tissue. Medically it is used to help other drugs and fluids spread through tissue, for example alongside local anesthetics in eye surgery and for fluids given under the skin.

name: Philtrum filler / shortening
summary: Reshaping the philtrum and cupid's bow with filler or a lip lift to look shorter and more defined; plenty of cosmetic practice, little formal evidence.
lead: The philtrum is the vertical groove in the middle of the upper lip, running from the base of the nose to the lip's upper edge. The cupid's bow is the double curve of the upper lip's border, with peaks lining up with the philtral columns.

name: Lip bleaching / lightening laser
summary: Procedures, including lasers, aimed at lightening darker or pigmented lips; evidence specific to lips is scarce.
lead: Lip bleaching or lightening refers to cosmetic treatments intended to reduce darker pigmentation of the lips, using laser, topical agents or other methods.

name: Lemon and sugar lip lightening
summary: A DIY scrub of lemon juice and sugar used to lighten lips; untested for this purpose, and lemon juice plus sun can cause skin darkening.
lead: Lemon and sugar lip lightening is a home remedy in which lemon juice, usually combined with sugar granules, is applied to or rubbed on the lips with the aim of making them lighter.

name: Honey and beetroot lip remedies
summary: Folk remedies using honey or beetroot juice for lip color and softness; beetroot stains temporarily, and no lip studies exist.
lead: Honey and beetroot lip remedies are folk practices in which honey is applied to the lips for softness or beetroot juice is applied for a pink or red tint.

name: Vitamin E / coconut oil lips
summary: Home use of vitamin E oil or coconut oil on the lips for softness; plausible as a moisturizer but no lip-specific trials, and vitamin E can cause contact dermatitis.
lead: Vitamin E and coconut oil are commonly used in home lip care, applied for softness and to ease chapping.

name: Quitting smoking for lips
summary: Stopping tobacco is claimed to improve dark, thin, lined lips; general smoker's-face research exists, lip-specific research does not.
lead: Quitting smoking for lips is a lifestyle practice in which people stop using tobacco in the hope of reducing the dark, thin or lined appearance of the lips and the surrounding skin. It sits within the broader appearance-related idea of "smoker's face", a pattern of premature facial ageing that clinicians have described in people who smoke.
claims: Smoking makes lips darker and thinner, and quitting reverses this.
Quitting smoking reduces vertical lip lines ("smoker's lines").

name: Lip filler cannula technique
summary: Injecting lip filler with a blunt cannula instead of a needle is touted as gentler; no comparison was found in the sources reviewed.
lead: Lip filler cannula technique refers to injecting dermal filler into the lips through a blunt-tipped flexible tube (a cannula) rather than a sharp needle. Within appearance communities it is often described as a gentler or safer approach, mainly because proponents say it causes less bruising and lowers the chance of puncturing a blood vessel.
claims: Cannulas bruise less and are safer than needles.

name: Lipstick shade matching
summary: Choosing lipstick colour to suit skin tone and lip shape; history and safety are documented, attractiveness effects are untested.
lead: Lipstick shade matching is the cosmetic practice of choosing a lip colour to suit a person's skin tone, lip shape and overall look, and in appearance communities it is discussed as a way to emphasise lip shape and facial harmony. Lipstick itself is a wax-based colour product, and lip colour has been worn for thousands of years in many cultures.
claims: The right lipstick shade for your skin tone enhances lip shape and facial harmony.

name: PLLA / Sculptra perioral
summary: A collagen-stimulating injectable used around the mouth; perioral evidence in the sources reviewed is one ongoing trial.
lead: PLLA / Sculptra perioral refers to the use of poly-L-lactic acid, the active ingredient in the injectable product Sculptra, in the area around the mouth to stimulate collagen and soften wrinkles or restore volume. It is classed as a collagen stimulator rather than an immediate volumising filler.

name: Lip stencil / bone structure hack: orthotropics for lip support
summary: The claim that mewing reshapes bone to support the lips; reference sources call mewing unproven and do not cover lips.
lead: This entry covers the claim, circulated in mewing and orthotropics circles, that jaw and facial posture training can change the profile of the lips by altering the bone structure that supports them. Mewing is a form of oral posture training associated with orthodontist John Mew and his son Mike Mew, built on tongue pressure against the palate.
claims: Mewing can change lip profile by moving the underlying bone structure.

name: Lip competence training
summary: Keeping the lips sealed at rest as a posture habit; claimed to aid facial growth, untested as training.
lead: Lip competence training is the habit of keeping the lips gently sealed at rest, treated in some oral-posture communities as a posture skill that is said to support jaw and facial development. In orthodontics, lip competence is a clinical descriptor meaning the lips can close at rest without strain, and lip incompetence means they cannot.
claims: Keeping the lips sealed at rest improves jaw and facial development.

name: Cryolipolysis (CoolSculpting Mini Chin)
summary: Fat freezing under the chin: a cleared non-surgical option with modest measured fat reduction and a rare paradoxical-growth side effect.
lead: Cryolipolysis, commonly called fat freezing and sold under the CoolSculpting brand, is a non-invasive procedure that uses extreme cold applied to the skin to reduce subcutaneous fat in targeted areas . The submental area under the chin is one of the sites for which the US FDA has cleared the technique, alongside the jawline, arms, flanks, abdomen and thighs .

name: Lipodissolve / PC-DC injections
summary: Injected fat-dissolving mixtures (phosphatidylcholine/deoxycholate) that have drawn FDA warnings; the only approved injectable is a separate deoxycholic acid product.
lead: Lipodissolve, also called injection lipolysis or PC/DC injections, refers to injecting drug mixtures into subcutaneous fat to destroy fat cells. Most formulations are based on phosphatidylcholine (PC) and sodium deoxycholate (DC) . Practitioners have used it for small localized deposits, including under the chin.

name: Laser lipolysis (SmartLipo)
summary: Laser-assisted fat removal that heats fat through a small cannula, with early studies reporting fat reduction and some skin tightening.
lead: Laser lipolysis, also called laser-assisted liposuction or by the SmartLipo brand, uses laser energy delivered through a thin fiber under the skin to disrupt fat cells, sometimes followed by suction removal. It is promoted for small areas, including the neck and jawline, and for tightening skin .

name: Body recomposition / calorie deficit
summary: Eating below maintenance to lose body fat, including from the face, usually paired with protein and lifting; fat loss cannot be targeted to the face.
lead: A calorie deficit occurs when energy intake is lower than total daily energy expenditure, so the body supplies the shortfall mainly from stored fat . Body recomposition is the related goal of reducing fat while maintaining or increasing lean mass, typically discussed alongside resistance training and higher protein intake .
claims: Losing body fat reveals the jaw and cheekbones.
Teens in puberty should not cut calories.
Higher protein with lifting preserves muscle in a cut.

name: Low-sodium / low-carb face de-bloat
summary: Cutting salt and carbs to shed facial water retention; the general link between sodium and fluid is documented, but no study tests it for facial appearance.
lead: Low-sodium and low-carb face de-bloating refers to adjusting diet, mainly salt and carbohydrate intake, to reduce fluid retention that practitioners say blurs facial definition. It is typically a short-term practice used before photos or events.

name: Face slimming massage / lymphatic drainage
summary: Facial massage and gua sha to move fluid and reduce puffiness; popular in forums, with no studies on facial slimming found.
lead: Face slimming massage refers to facial massage techniques, often adapted from manual lymphatic drainage (MLD), and tools such as gua sha used to reduce facial puffiness and improve definition. Proponents say the effect is fluid redistribution, not fat loss .
claims: Lymphatic congestion makes the face look puffy and blurs the jawline.
Daily facial massage and gua sha reduce face puffiness.

name: Chewing gum for face fat
summary: The idea that chewing gum melts cheek fat; it rests on spot reduction, which exercise research does not support, and no trial tests it.
lead: Chewing gum for face fat is the belief, found in appearance-focused online communities, that repeatedly chewing gum burns fat in the cheeks and jaw area or slims the face. It belongs to the wider family of facial-slimming ideas that assume working a local muscle will reduce the fat over it.
